segments: and a great tumor {OCR?} developed in him.
And more than what he said to the slave,
"If your intention is to kill me, let me know,"
he did not add anything else.
And after Saladin died,
Buktamar, the ruler of Khilat, heard [of it],
and he rejoiced with great joy,
and began to gather forces to come against Mayperqat.
Then a man named Hazārdīnārī,
who was also one of the slaves of the Shāh-i Arman,
rose up against him and killed him,
and ruled in his place.
And because he was Buktamar's son-in-law,
he did not kill the young son whom he had,
whose name was Muhammad,
but reared him as his own child.
And in that same year, Sinān, the head of the Ismailites, died in Masyāf (or Misryāt):
and there arose in his place a Persian man named Nāṣir.
For Sinān was feared by all the kings of the Arabs and of the Franks,
and he used to prepare daggers,
and on each one of them [inscribed] the name of one of the kings.
And when he gave a dagger to one of his followers,
even into the heart of the sea he would enter and fulfill his will.
For he had become skilled in the wisdom of the ancients,
and the transmigration of souls—
that is, the Platonic doctrine—
he taught to his followers.
And therefore they despised death,
and [believed] that they did not depart from the world, even if they were killed.
And at times he would conceal himself,
and the report would go out that he had died,
and then he would reveal himself again.
And because of this,
even when he died, his men did not believe that he was dead.
And in that same year,
which is the year one thousand five hundred and four,
1504 of the Greeks [1192–1193 AD],
Leo, the ruler (prince) of Cilicia, acted craftily,
and captured Prince Bohemond, the lord of Antioch.
For while Baghras was in Leo's possession,
as we have said above,
which, when the Arabs abandoned it and fled,
he had taken,
he instructed the Armenian governor of Baghras to plot a secret scheme with the Prince:
that he wished to rebel against his lord Leo,
and surrender the fortress to the Prince,
and enter and dwell in Antioch.
And when that governor sent word to the Prince,
and promised that he would deliver Baghras to him,
the Prince believed him.
And he went out as if hunting,
and with him also his son and his wife.
And when they came and encamped at the spring in front of Baghras,
